_about: How a parsed street address is put in one standard form, so the same place written different ways is one StreetAddress. libpostal splits the address into parts. Each part is lowercased; letters with no decomposition are written as the letters table writes them (ICAO Doc 9303's transliteration of Latin letters); accents on Latin letters are dropped, while marks on letters of other scripts are kept since they change the letter; and punctuation becomes spaces. The words and phrases in forms are then replaced by their standard forms for the countries listed: in the street by position (first: the type before the name; last: after it, or before a trailing directional; any: wherever the words stand; ending: the end of a word, as in compound street names), and in the unit and PO box. A country's forms come from its postal operator or from the Universal Postal Union's list of thoroughfare types and abbreviations, with the page cited. Postal codes are written the first way the country's postal code pattern accepts (patterns from the pioz/countries data), except where postcodes below keep only the first digits. The identity of a Location is its number, street, unit, PO box, city, province, postal code and country in this form; a building name counts only when there is no street. Add countries and words here, not in Go code.
